Stagewatch.summary:
Stagewatch is the Show Bus hub. It holds the master spec, broadcasts a `t:"main"` hello on UDP 9928 and hears every kind of node there. It serves numbered frames (/ws, /api/state), receipts (HTTP X-Request-Id, WS id, Companion @id), clock pings, its own context (GET /api/context, MCP get_context), a store for peer contexts (POST /api/peers/context, kept 30 s), scoped keys including the `node` scope, TLS on the same port 9924, and the shared approval queue (/api/proposals…). The 2.17 windows appear in its context as `window:<name>` items of kind `screen`.

Stagewatch makes an outbound Show Bus connection to one app only: Patterns. PatternsLink opens a TCP link to a configured host:9697. It pairs with HELLO, then NONCE→AUTH-PROOF (plain AUTH when no NONCE comes). It sends a whitelist of VIDEO verbs with @ids, timed PINGs and `@ctx CONTEXT` every 5 s, and reads STATE.video, receipts, PONG and the context. That link has no TLS or STARTTLS.

AGMessage, PlayMap and Patterns reach Stagewatch by pulling and pushing to it: /ws, POST /api/peers/context, /api/proposals collect and result, and for AGMessage POST /api/message with a node key. Stagewatch never calls AGMessage or PlayMap. It has no PlayMap-specific code at all. A PlayMap hello (`t:"playmap"`) is accepted only because any token kind is heard, and it is shown under the raw kind "playmap". PlayMap's context, its proposals and its /ws connection go through the generic paths. As a side effect, every peer that opens /ws with cid/page shows up in Stagewatch's Screens list and receives `screen go/identify/reload/disconnect` messages.

Stagewatch's own copilot cannot propose lines for another node; only proposals arriving over HTTP can target one. Windows can show only Stagewatch's own pages. A node key cannot see window addresses. Frames and the hello carry nothing about windows. So no peer can use a window yet.

Stagewatch.canShowWebPages:
Stagewatch cannot put an arbitrary web page or browser source on its own outputs. Its output window is WPF with NDI. It uses WebView2 only to host its bundled holographic page on the virtual host 'stagewatch-holo.local', as a layer that steps aside when it stalls (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Output/HoloHost.cs:14-29; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Output/Timer.Output.csproj:21).

Its "windows" work the other way round: Stagewatch serves GET /w/<token> pages that any browser opens (a TV, an OBS or vMix browser input, a signage player) and drives what they show (Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:252-300). Window content is limited to Stagewatch's own pages. ScreenPreset.ValidPath refuses '://' and '//' (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/AppSettings.cs:305-308). ScreenWindows.CanShow and ResolveContent allow only Stagewatch pages, setups, holding or black (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ScreenWindows.cs:121-161). The window CSP has frame-src 'self' (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:621-622). So a Patterns, PlayMap or AGMessage page cannot be shown in a Stagewatch window.

For a peer to show a Stagewatch window as a browser source it would need the /w/<token> address. GET /api/windows gives the path only to the PIN or a control key, never a node key (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:679,689). Stagewatch/docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:99-100 says: "Patterns and PlayMap could take a window address as a browser source; nothing there does yet."
openIssues: Stagewatch/docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:87-103 (2.17, what the round did not do): no window feedbacks in Companion because frames carry no windows block; no QR for a window's address; window content is a page path resolved when the command runs; 'Patterns and PlayMap could take a window address as a browser source; nothing there does yet'; the window fail-safe has no timer of its own on the server.

PlayMap is not in the contract: Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:37 lists the kinds main/agent/patterns/messenger and the §8 table (:143-148) has no PlayMap row. The Patterns and AGMessage copies (Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md, AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md) do not mention playmap either. Stagewatch/src has no PlayMap code; the Show network label map lacks 'playmap' (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:100).

Stale docs in Stagewatch/docs/NODES.md. :22 says the id is 'stable for the node's run', but it is install-stable (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/SettingsStore.cs:201-202). :72-74 describes the pre-1.1 Patterns link (AUTH <token>, PING, 7 s drop); the code uses proof pairing and 12 s (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:42-47). :97 says 'Stagewatch ignores kinds it doesn't know', but every kind is now heard (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/RemoteSlides.cs:185-186). :99-101 describes AGMessage using pin= and a control key; AGMessage now sends a node key in a Bearer header (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:317-319,366).

The hello is broadcast only to 255.255.255.255 with no loopback send (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/RemoteSlides.cs:167), while Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:27 says broadcast and loopback. It is also sent when the web server is bound to loopback only (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Slides.cs:21; Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:957), against Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:45.
The Patterns link has no TLS or STARTTLS and pins no certificate (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:192-199), although Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:182-184 allows STARTTLS on the wire.

Patterns command outcome: Stagewatch journals the action at send time and gives its own sender only an 'accepted' receipt. Patterns' real OK or ERR reaches only the status line (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:64-66,86-88; Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Receipts.cs:48-52).

Stagewatch's own copilot cannot propose to other nodes. CopilotStep has no target (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/Copilot.cs:23) and only HTTP calls ProposalDesk.Submit (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:31). Stagewatch/docs/ECOSYSTEM.md:141-149 still lists as 'Then/Later': the cross-node approval queue in Stagewatch's copilot, merged journals and report, one preflight, ecosystem failover, chaos rehearsal, one Companion module.
No manifest at /.well-known/show-node.json, which Stagewatch/docs/ECOSYSTEM.md:39-41 plans; no such route in Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:395-566.

Peer apps that open /ws (Patterns cid=patterns, AGMessage cid=agmessage, PlayMap page=/playmap) are listed as browser screens. A `screen go|identify|reload|disconnect` with no target or 'all' reaches them (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/Screens.cs:61-68; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:77-131,1191-1200).

AcceptPeerContext ignores a refused BindKey, so a node key already bound to one node can still post a context under another node's id (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:65-70).

Context gaps. Windows are added to Links, so each gets a timer→window link of kind 'hears' (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Show/ShowContext.cs:126; Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:62). The context's commands list omits patterns play/pause/stop/seek/restart and most window actions (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Show/ShowContext.cs:28-45). The hello has no 'windows' cap (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Slides.cs:36).

Windows are closed to peers: a node key gets no window path (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:679,689), and a node key cannot run the 'window' verb directly; only message and clearmessage are allowed (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ApiKeys.cs:84-85). A peer must propose window lines to the desk for approval.

Outbound HTTP triggers send no auth header or request id (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/Triggers.cs:131-139), so they cannot drive Patterns, AGMessage or PlayMap with a key without putting a secret in the URL.

Patterns.summary:
Patterns already does most of Show Bus 1.1 and 1.2 toward Stagewatch, and none of it toward PlayMap or AGMessage beyond hearing their hellos.

How it reaches Stagewatch:
- It is an optional client, off by default (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Model/ShowState.cs:2342), turned on from the Nodes page only (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Views/Sections/NodesSection.axaml:103-119). No wire verb configures the link.
- It dials the first live hello with t="main", or a typed host:port. It opens ws(s)://host:port/ws?cid=patterns&page=/patterns with "Authorization: Bearer swk_…".
- Every 2 s it sends {"cmd":"ping","t":…}. Every 5 s it reads GET /api/context and posts its own context to POST /api/peers/context.
- When the hello lists cap `approvals` it posts and collects proposals at /api/proposals.
- Over TLS it pins the certificate on first use (CERTIFICATE CHANGED until ACCEPT).

What it does with what it reads:
- Only "state" and "pong" WebSocket messages are used. The state frames drive one-room-one-timer: /stage, /timer, STAGE STATUS, STATE.stage, the timer nodes by twin relay. TIMER PAUSE/RESUME/ADD are refused while following.
- The Stagewatch context is drawn on the Eye's CONTROL plane and goes into the assistant's brief.
- STATE gains a `bus` row, and the Companion module has variables for it.
- Patterns never sends Stagewatch a show command or a stage message. Its proposals always target itself.

How it serves Stagewatch (Stagewatch is the client of Patterns' wire on TCP 9697):
- On connect: a STATE greeting, then NONCE <hex>. The client answers AUTH-PROOF = HMAC-SHA256(normalised token, nonce + HELLO name); plain AUTH works on loopback only.
- `@id` receipts (OK @id / ERR @id), and PING t1 answered OK PONG t1 t2 t3.
- CONTEXT is a query, open without pairing. STATE goes whole to every wire peer on each change, paired or not.
- Stagewatch's `patterns end/restart/play/pause/stop/seek` (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:126-147) map one to one to VIDEO END n / RESTART / PLAY / PAUSE / STOP / SEEK n (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ControlProtocol.cs:777-819). A bare number of seconds is accepted for SEEK (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/WebVt.cs:76-80).
- PAUSE and STOP refuse a playlist item or a stinger, and only the clip on air can be driven (L48, L49).

PlayMap: not mentioned anywhere in Patterns (src, tests, docs). Its hello (t="playmap") is drawn as a generic grey "Playmap" app, never linked and its context never read. The only path toward it is the generic Interactive-area device (DEVICE <name> <line>, fact lines out).

AGMessage: the hello is heard and drawn as a violet card. Patterns never reads AGMessage's /api/context, although AGMessage's own comment expects "Patterns' Eye" to read it (AGMessage/app/server.js:298).

Showing a Stagewatch window on a Patterns output — yes in principle, Windows only:
- A web page is a picture source through WebView2, rendered off-screen and captured by screencast. It can be a Media → Web pattern, a Web layer, or a Confidence/Info screen's own picture. At most 4 pages at once.
- It can be set from the desk (Media page), or as a saved-page Library tile on the wire (`SCREEN n PVW LIBRARY <tile>` then a take). `WEB OPEN <url> [ON <page>]` only re-points a page already mounted.
- No wire verb adds a new address. Nothing in Patterns knows about Stagewatch windows.

Interop gaps found in this read (not in OPEN.md):
1. Stagewatch signals a stuck show thread with {"type":"beat","live":false} (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1264-1270,1297). Patterns reads `live` only from a state frame (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/StagewatchFollow.cs:43-44,61). A beat refreshes the link's last word but is otherwise ignored (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:521-538). So the promised "a stuck Stagewatch shows no time" (Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:645) cannot happen against a real Stagewatch: the link stays live and keeps counting on from the last frame. The test only proves a state-frame shape Stagewatch never sends (Patterns/tests/Patterns.Core.Tests/ShowBusTests.cs:374).
2. STATE's `web.url` carries the full address of the page on air (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/CommandRouter.cs:301,306). STATE is pushed to every wire peer, paired or not, over plain TCP (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ControlService.cs:60,356-358,763-774). A Stagewatch /w/<token> shown on Patterns would therefore leak the window token, which Stagewatch's doctrine says rides in no frame.
3. WebFrameSource handles no ServerCertificateErrorDetected event, so an https:// window address on Stagewatch's self-signed certificate is left to WebView2's default handling.
4. The cid is fixed at "patterns" (StagewatchLinkService.cs:276), so two desks would share one Stagewatch Screen id (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1194). Screen commands arriving on that socket are ignored.
5. The context's `commands` list lacks VIDEO STOP (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowContext.cs:157-173), so an approval desk would treat it as high risk.
6. The Eye draws links only inside one app's own context (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/Eye.cs:812-819). A Patterns screen showing a Stagewatch window cannot be drawn as "shows" that window item.

Patterns.canShowWebPages:
Yes, on Windows only. Nothing in Patterns is built for Stagewatch windows.

How a web page gets on an output:
- A page is a picture source rendered by WebView2 in a window kept off every screen. Frames arrive by Chromium's screencast, with a 20 fps screenshot fallback. The browser is started with occlusion and timer throttling off, so a countdown page keeps running (Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/WebFrameSource.cs:15-62; class at :26 is [SupportedOSPlatform("windows")]).
- It can be the pattern (Media → Web, MediaSource.Web at Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Model/Enums.cs:185-186; WebUrl/WebWidth/WebHeight/WebZoomPct at Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Model/PatternConfig.cs:458-464). playmap (repo Mapper).summary:
PlayMap is a full Show Bus 1.2 node of kind "playmap". Every 2 s it sends a hello to UDP 9928 with 16 caps and its ports (http/ws/https 9940, wire 9941, sync 9942), and it listens to every hello.

It joins Stagewatch as a SCREEN, not as a window. Its StagewatchLink (LINK STAGEWATCH host[:9924] [swk_ key], or "" for the first 'main' it hears) opens Stagewatch's /ws?cid=<nodeId>&page=/playmap&detail=1 with Authorization: Bearer <key>. It reads state frames into a 'timer:' picture source (time in the phase colour, title and message only). It sends {"cmd":"ping","t"} every 2 s for the clock offset, which is measured but used by nothing. It handles redirect/identify/reload/disconnect: identify runs OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5; redirect is only remembered as words. With a key it POSTs its §6 context to /api/peers/context every 5 s. When the Stagewatch hello has the 'approvals' cap it pulls GET /api/proposals?target=<id>&state=approved every 2 s, runs each line once through its own gate and POSTs /api/proposals/<id>/result {ok,words}. Its proposer side (StagewatchProposalSink: POST /api/proposals) is written and tested but never switched on in production.

To Patterns, PlayMap dials the line wire (9697) the way Stagewatch does: HELLO PlayMap, AUTH-PROOF, PING every 2 s, CONTEXT every 5 s. It reads the STATE video row and the blackout, and follows the blackout.

PlayMap serves Patterns' line grammar on TCP 9941 (HELLO Stagewatch is labelled transport 'stagewatch'), HTTP POST /api/cmd, a screens' /ws with JSON receipts, MCP and OSC /playmap/line. Pairing is by token proof, a trusted address, loopback, or an open node. STATE's 'video' row has Patterns' shape, so Stagewatch's existing VT link to Patterns works against PlayMap when typed in by hand at port 9941. Stagewatch's finder only accepts t:"patterns", so it does not find PlayMap by itself.

Playback verbs a controller can send:
- VIDEO PLAY/PAUSE/STOP/RESTART/SEEK/END/RATE (aliases VT, CLIP)
- PLAYLIST GO/CUE/NEXT/PREV/FOCUS, with AT +ms|<unix ms> and EXPECT
- TIMECODE CHASE/ENGAGE/INTERNAL, BLACKOUT, MASTER, PANIC
- OUTPUT SOURCE / SURFACE SOURCE (e.g. timer:)

AT <unix ms> is read on PlayMap's own show clock. No offset from Stagewatch's clock is applied, and nothing follows a Stagewatch countdown as time (Stagewatch LTC over the bus is not built).

PlayMap cannot render a web page. MediaKind.Web exists, but the media backend returns no picture for it and no browser engine is referenced. So a Stagewatch window (/w/<token>) cannot be put on a projector directly, except through an NDI/OMT/Spout feed from something that renders the page. PlayMap does not speak Stagewatch's window link (?win=<token>, {"type":"window"} frames).

AGMessage is absent from Mapper. Its hello (t:"messenger") would only show as a grey peer "heard at <address>".

playmap (repo Mapper).canShowWebPages:
No. PlayMap has no browser engine:
- MediaKind.Web exists ("A web page, rendered by the browser engine", Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Model/MediaModel.cs:11-12).
- MEDIA IMPORT of an http(s) URL adds a Web item and answers "added" (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/EngineCore.Content.cs:395-404).
- But MediaBackend.Open returns null for Web and Embed ("pages and embeds are another renderer's", Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/MediaBackend.cs:144-145), and no CefSharp, WebView2 or Chromium package is referenced anywhere in Mapper.
- Web pages as a source class are a roadmap item only (Mapper/docs/ROADMAP.md:726, L10; CEF off-screen researched in Mapper/docs/RESEARCH.md:107-109).

So a Stagewatch window (GET /w/<token>) cannot be put on a PlayMap projector directly. PlayMap also does not speak Stagewatch's window link (/ws?win=<token>, {"type":"window"} frames); its StagewatchLink connects only as a screen with cid/page=/playmap/detail=1 (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:284) and ignores unknown message types (:431-432).

There are two routes today:
1. Native: SourceKind.Timer draws Stagewatch's state frames as a picture (time in the phase colour, title, message) on any surface or output (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/TimerView.cs:10-15,131-150; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/EngineSources.cs:178-179). It is not the HTML window.
2. Indirect: another app renders the page and sends it as NDI, OMT or Spout, which PlayMap takes as a live input (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Media/LiveVideo.cs:7-12; Mapper/docs/VIDEO.md:1-6).
openIssues: StagewatchProposalSink is not switched on: UseApprovalDeskAsync is called with options only in tests, and in production only with null (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Assistant/AssistantService.cs:141-157,273). The carry-over says 'StagewatchProposalSink not switched on (StagewatchLink already collects approved lines; must set CollectApproved=false) → fleet/showsafety decides' (Mapper/docs/round2/CARRYOVER.md:99). PlayMap's own assistant cannot send proposals to a Stagewatch desk.

A Stagewatch 'redirect' does not change the picture. NetworkHost stores the view (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:785-788) and uses it only in STATE detail words (:309-316); TimerView draws one fixed layout. This contradicts Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:37 ('pick which Stagewatch view PlayMap renders').

The timer picture drops contract fields. StagewatchTimerJson carries only state, text, seconds, phase, color, title, message, trusted and why (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:318-341), and TimerView reads only text, color, title and message (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/TimerView.cs:131-150). So watermark (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchTimer.cs:55: 'Must be shown whenever it is not empty'), holding, flash, urgency, next and playout are not shown, although Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:49-50 claims them.

Stagewatch windows are not supported: no ?win=<token> join, no {"type":"window"} handling, no /w/ rendering (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:284,431-432; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1142-1145,1290).
Web pages are not rendered: MediaKind.Web imports but plays nothing (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/MediaBackend.cs:144-145). It is a roadmap item, not built (Mapper/docs/ROADMAP.md:726, L10).

Link clock offsets are measured but unused: StagewatchLink.Clock and the PatternsLink/WireClient Clock have no consumer in PlayMap.Engine. AT <unix ms> is read on PlayMap's own show clock (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/EngineCore.Router.cs:253-272), so a controller that sends absolute instants from its own clock is off by the clock difference between the machines.
Stagewatch LTC over the Show Bus is not built (Mapper/docs/ROADMAP.md:650, R3.7). TIMECODE SOURCE takes LTC, MTC, ARTNET and INTERNAL only (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Wire/VerbCatalog.cs:398).

Show Bus 1.3 proposals wait on the other apps (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:67-89): the node kind 'playmap' in the contract; Patterns hello→device; Patterns reading third-party contexts; Patterns destinations; Stagewatch's finder accepting t:"playmap" (today it accepts only t=='patterns', Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:459); a video.anchor cap and ANCHOR line; and an Eye command cap of at least 256 (Mapper/docs/round2/CARRYOVER.md:55-67).
/api/context stays behind the token by the owner's answer 'Keep it closed' (Mapper/docs/round2/CARRYOVER.md:53-54). Peers read PlayMap's context over the wire's CONTEXT or SUBSCRIBE CONTEXT.

Context size margin: the busy golden context is 43,640 bytes (Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Engine.Tests/Fleet/Golden/context-busy.json). Stagewatch refuses a peer context over 64 KB (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:456), and round 3 adds about 20 more command rows (Mapper/docs/round2/CARRYOVER.md:57-59). No test was found that holds the context under Stagewatch's limit.
A typed Stagewatch address that no hello matches never collects approvals: Approvals defaults to false (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:726-734).

STATE links.stagewatch.paired means only 'Live', not that the key is accepted (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:315). A refused context post appears only in the detail words (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:510-513).

Patterns' clip clock is read but drives nothing in PlayMap's playback; it is shown as links.patterns.clip and detail only (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:293-307; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/StateWriter.cs:499-500).
AGMessage: no integration and no doc mention in Mapper. AGMessage shows up only as a grey 'messenger' peer (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:283-290; AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:73).

AGMessage (Node.js messenger node, app 0.canShowWebPages:
No. AGMessage has no display outputs. It is a set of web pages served on port 3023 (AGMessage/app/server.js:235-237) that people open in a browser. Neither side can host the other's pages:
- AGMessage cannot frame another node's page: its CSP allows frames only from itself and blob: (AGMessage/app/lib/guard.js:109).
- Other sites cannot frame AGMessage: its CSP sets frame-ancestors 'self' and it sends X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN (AGMessage/app/lib/guard.js:113,120).
- A Stagewatch window will not show AGMessage either: `window show` refuses other sites (Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:275,296).
The only screen-like thing it does is hold a /ws link that Stagewatch lists as a screen named 'agmessage' with page '/agmessage' (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:317; Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1195-1196). It ignores any screen commands sent on that link (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:325-332).
openIssues: There is no OPEN.md, CARRYOVER.md or WHATS_NEXT.md in AGMessage (the repo root has only README.md, README.txt, CHANGELOG.md and docs/{NODES,SHOWBUS}.md), and there are no TODO or FIXME markers in app/*.js, app/lib or app/public outside vendor. The items below come from reading the code against the contract and Stagewatch's code.

Defect: the proposed stage-message line `message "<text>" <urgency> ack` (AGMessage/app/server.js:703) is invalid in Stagewatch's grammar. The third argument is the flash rate (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowState.cs:750-756), and 'ack' throws in ParseFlash (ShowState.cs:1187-1193). The desk rates it 'high' (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:76-80) and fails it on approval (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:146-155). It should be `message "…" <urgency> off ack`, matching the direct path in AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:374. The test pins the wrong line (AGMessage/app/test/server.test.js:336).

PlayMap is invisible: the KINDS filter in AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:33 drops the t:'playmap' hello (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:13). There is no PlayMap context read, label (AGMessage/app/public/admin-plus.js:72) or proposal target. Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:67-69 proposes adding the 'playmap' kind to the contract in Show Bus 1.3.

Patterns: no direct link (no wire on 9697, no AUTH-PROOF, no CONTEXT or /api/context read, no proposals aimed at Patterns). The only Patterns facts AGMessage gets come from Stagewatch's context peers (AGMessage/app/lib/context.js:112-115).

Stagewatch windows are not consumed: no GET /api/windows, no window verb, and the window:<name> items in Stagewatch's context are ignored because only headline, light and peers are read (AGMessage/app/lib/context.js:71-78,103-117; AGMessage/app/server.js:860). AGMessage's node key cannot run window verbs (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ApiKeys.cs:85); only a desk proposal could, and AGMessage makes none.

§11 report retry gap: if POST /api/proposals/<id>/result fails, AGMessage never sends it again. The retry happens only when the proposal is collected again (AGMessage/app/server.js:1097-1101), but Stagewatch hands out each approved proposal once (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:141-143) and marks it undelivered after 5 min (Approvals.cs:46,185).

Stagewatch's description of AGMessage is stale: Stagewatch/docs/NODES.md:94-101 still says AGMessage sends a top-level `web:3023`, listens on 9700, puts the key in `pin=` in the WS URL and uses a control key. AGMessage 0.3 and later use ports.http, no 9700 (AGMessage/CHANGELOG.md:43), the key in a header (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:319-320) and a node key (AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:10).
Spec copy drift: AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:167 says the certificate lasts 'five years'; the master Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:166-167 says 825 days, which is what AGMessage's code does.
The ping cadence is 1 s in code (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:221,350-354) but documented as every 2 s (AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:10).

The TLS pin is confirmed on the first 'state' frame (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:329). Stagewatch sends the public frame even to a client whose key is invalid when no viewing code is set (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1154-1164), so this is not strictly 'first authenticated use' as AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:10 claims. A wrong key also still shows 'connected'.

Every AGMessage install dials Stagewatch with the same cid=agmessage (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:317), so two AGMessages share one Screens id on Stagewatch (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1195).

The hello caps 'action-prompts', 'documents' and 'proposals' (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:34) are not in the contract's caps vocabulary (AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:43). 'proposals' means 'I propose', not 'I keep a queue'.

AGMessage keeps no approval queue of its own (§11 says that with no desk each app approves its own). Without a Stagewatch desk, the 📝 propose button is hidden (canPropose, AGMessage/app/server.js:489) and the notice verb cannot be reached.

How to read this: capabilities[] lists the master's normative rules (§1 to §11), one per entry. `status` says how far the four apps match the rule: implemented means no contradiction was found, partial means at least one app's own docs (or code, where checked) contradict it, absent means no app does it. `peer` names the app that contradicts or that the rule is about. Evidence is repo-relative path:line. This was a read-only pass: nothing was edited, built or run.

1. DIFF OF THE THREE SHOWBUS.md COPIES (whitespace ignored)
- (a) The copy headers are not substantive. Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md:1 adds "this is Patterns' copy, round 88 (Show Bus 1.2), word for word but for the name of the language model". AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:1 adds "Master copy: Stagewatch … where they differ, the master wins". The master states that it is the master at Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:6.
- (b) §9, first table row. The master (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:154) and AGMessage (AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:156) say "Claude: copilot plans…". Patterns (Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md:156) says "The language model: …". This is a deliberate local edit in Patterns, not an older or newer text. Patterns' wording is the one that meets both trees' rule "No model or tool identifiers in anything pushed" (Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md and Patterns/CLAUDE.md, "Constraints that bite"). The master breaks its own repository's rule here.
- (c) §10, certificate lifetime. The master (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:166-168) and Patterns (Patterns/docs/SHOWBUS.md:168-169) say "ECDSA P-256, 825 days — Apple devices refuse longer — renewed 30 days before it ends". AGMessage (AGMessage/docs/SHOWBUS.md:168) says "ECDSA P-256, five years;" and drops the Apple and renewal clauses. The master and Patterns are newer on this point:
  - AGMessage's own code says so: AGMessage/app/lib/tls.js:12 reads "825 days, not the five years the contract suggests", and tls.js:72 uses days = 825.
  - AGMessage/docs/NODES.md:8 and AGMessage/CHANGELOG.md:8-9 also say 825 days.
  - Git cannot order the copies. Each has a single commit on 2026-10-11: Stagewatch cb5fa69 at 04:06, AGMessage f0e0851 at 04:12, Patterns ce96fc8 at 04:13. Patterns and Mapper are shallow clones.
- Those three are the only differences. Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md is not a copy. It is PlayMap's own node page, which claims 1.2 and proposes "Show Bus 1.3" changes (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:67-89).

2. IS PLAYMAP NAMED IN THE MASTER? No. A case-insensitive grep for playmap and mapper over all three SHOWBUS.md copies found nothing (exit 1).
- The title names only "Stagewatch, Patterns, AGMessage and their micro-apps" (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:1).
- The §2 hello-kind table lists only main, agent, patterns and messenger (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:37).
- The §8 publish/consume table has rows only for Stagewatch, Patterns, AGMessage and the Slides agent (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:143-148).
- Stagewatch/docs/ECOSYSTEM.md never names PlayMap either (grep exit 1).
- Inside Stagewatch, PlayMap appears only in Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md ("Part of the Patterns ecosystem with Patterns, PlayMap (repo Mapper) and AGMessage") and Stagewatch/docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:100.
- PlayMap asks for the kind `playmap` and its caps to be added (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:69-70).

3. CONTRADICTIONS THAT MATTER MOST for Stagewatch talking to AGMessage, PlayMap and Patterns
- (i) AGMessage drops every hello whose `t` is not main, agent, patterns or messenger (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:33,38). A PlayMap node is therefore invisible to AGMessage, even though AGMessage/CHANGELOG.md:43 says "every kind heard".
- (ii) Stagewatch's Patterns finder accepts only t:"patterns" (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:459). PlayMap is reached only by typing its address (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:36,81-82).
- (iii) Patterns reads only Stagewatch's context (Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:639). Its context reader keeps at most 64 commands (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowContext.cs:99). PlayMap asks for at least 256, stated in the spec (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:85-89).
- (iv) No app uses Stagewatch windows. A grep for `win=` and `/w/` in the Patterns, Mapper and AGMessage sources and docs found nothing. PlayMap uses the older Screens mechanism instead (`cid=<id>&page=/playmap`; Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:37 and Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:284).
- (v) The window address `/w/<token>` is a pass carried in a URL (Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:254-256). This breaks §1 rule 5, "Secrets ride in no URL". So do Stagewatch's `?pin=` and `?pin=swk_…` (Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:33,107,127,212).
- (vi) Certificate lifetime:
  - Patterns' code makes a 5-year certificate (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowBusTls.cs:84), and Patterns/docs/PLAN.md:11972 says "five years", although Patterns' own copy of the spec says 825 days.
  - AGMessage's copy says five years, but AGMessage's code uses 825.
- (vii) Stagewatch/docs/NODES.md is stale against the master on the hello fields, `id`, `proto`, the 9700 beacon, liveness timings, the AGMessage key and the node scope (details per rule below).
- (viii) Show data is readable without pairing on the line wires of both Patterns and PlayMap, against §1 rule 4:
  - Patterns pushes STATE on connect and answers STATE, STATUS and CONTEXT unpaired (Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:17-18,38-41; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/ControlService.cs:501).
  - PlayMap's queries STATE and CONTEXT are open, and STATE is pushed on HELLO (Mapper/docs/WIRE.md:89-91,98).

4. THE MASTER'S OWN INCONSISTENCIES
- `proto` defines no value for 1.2 (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:38).
- The §2 caps list omits `approvals` (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:41), although the header (lines 3-4) and §11 (line 188) add it.
- The §2 `ports` list omits `https`, which §10 adds (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:171). It also omits `companion`, which Stagewatch itself sends (Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Slides.cs:45).
- The §2 hello example has no `tls` (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:31-32).
- §4 gives `seq` two meanings: "increases with every published change" and "a seq that changes on every discontinuity" (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:73-75).
- §8 omits the flows 1.2 added: Patterns posting its context and proposals to Stagewatch (Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:613-618), every target collecting approved proposals, `/tls`, and windows.
- §6 sets no cap on items or commands.
- No hello size or field limits are set, and the readers differ:
  - Stagewatch: 2048 bytes, kind up to 16, id up to 40, 16 caps (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/RemoteSlides.cs:179,183,187).
  - Patterns: 4096 bytes, 32 caps (Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowBusNetwork.cs:130,147).
  - AGMessage: 4096 bytes, 20 caps (AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:83,47).
  - PlayMap: 2048 bytes (Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Bus/ShowBus.cs, HelloMaxBytes).
  - PlayMap's hello sits exactly at Stagewatch's 16-cap limit (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:15-16,21).
